version.changelog:
Initial release of gh-envcheck.

- Provides API to verify if required environment variables and CLI binaries are available.
- Supports both hosted API and standalone FastAPI app modes.
- Responds with lists of present and missing environment variables and binaries.
- Useful as a pre-flight environment check for deploying or running skills.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions are consistent with its stated purpose (checking presence of env var names and binaries); no signs of hidden behavior, though the docs contain minor inconsistencies and using the hosted API could reveal whether specific environment variables exist.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the code: the FastAPI app checks whether requested env var names exist (returns names, not values) and whether binaries are on PATH. The SKILL.md advertises a hosted API endpoint (https://api.greenhelix.net) that is not linked to a homepage or owner info — this is an external dependency users should verify. Also the standalone run example uses an incorrect module path (products.envcheck.envcheck.app) that doesn't match the provided package (envcheck.app), indicating sloppy docs but not malicious behavior.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions stay within scope: they tell the agent to call the API or run a local FastAPI server and only check lists of env var names and binary names. The instructions do not ask the agent to read arbitrary files or secret values. Caveat: calling the hosted API transmits the list of env var names you want checked to a third party, which can leak information about what you consider sensitive.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No formal install spec (instruction-only), which is low risk. The SKILL.md suggests pip installing fastapi/uvicorn and running uvicorn — reasonable for a local run. The mistaken import path in the run command is an inconsistency and will prevent the server from starting as documented unless corrected.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no credentials and the code only tests presence of environment variable names (os.environ.get(var) != None) and uses shutil.which to find binaries. It does not return env var values or read files. However, returning whether a particular env var exists can still leak sensitive information (e.g., presence of AWS-related vars) if you query the hosted endpoint or share the required_env list.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no persistent privileges, does not set always:true, and does not modify other skills or system configuration. It only exposes a simple HTTP endpoint when run.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: verify whether named env vars are set and whether binaries exist on PATH. Before using it: (1) Prefer running the provided code locally rather than sending env var names to the advertised hosted API — the hosted domain (api.greenhelix.net) and ownership are not documented, so sending lists of env var names could reveal what secrets or services you use. (2) If you run locally, correct the uvicorn import path to envcheck.app:app. (3) Avoid checking for highly revealing env var names (e.g., AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY) against unknown external services. (4) If you need a hosted service, verify the operator/trustworthiness and their privacy policy first.
